concepts.label: Auditing (Server security facility)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - rotation requests are themselves an audited action

concepts.label: Secrets Management
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - opens secrets: namespace. The page's own named Enterprise-Edition feature: writing Couchbase-Server-defined secrets to disk in encrypted format, via a distinct key-derivation hierarchy from the one manage-native-encryption-at-rest.md describes for bucket/audit/config/log DATA (see cross_component_finding - this is a genuinely separate mechanism, not a restatement of native encryption at rest, though both are rooted in the same master password).

concepts.label: System Secret
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - 'Couchbase Server-defined' items this facility protects: 'system-essential passwords and certificates'. Distinct from any single certificate/password concept elsewhere in the registry - this is the umbrella class Secrets Management operates on.

concepts.label: Master Key
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - derived from the master password via PBKDF2; distinct from encryption:master-password itself (the human-supplied secret) and from secrets:data-key (what the master key in turn protects).

concepts.label: Data Key (Secrets Management)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a randomly generated key, encrypted by the master key, that actually encrypts all system secrets on disk. NOT the same concept as encryption:data-encryption-key (the DEK from manage-native-encryption-at-rest.md/native-encryption-at-rest-overview.md, which encrypts bucket/audit/config/log DATA) - no page states the two are the same artifact, and they sit under two different encryption hierarchies rooted in the same master password. Kept apart per the no-silent-merge rule; flagged for SME review since the near-identical name and shared root secret make this an easy silent-merge trap.

concepts.label: Secrets rotation levels (master-password / data-key / secret)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - scheme, following the project's index-state precedent. The page's own three explicitly numbered levels ('the first level of rotation... the second level of rotation... the third level of rotation'), each with its own CLI/REST surface. Modeled as a flat scheme rather than three separate concepts since the page addresses them only as an ordered set, never singly.

cross_component_finding: This page describes a SECOND, independently-rooted encryption hierarchy from the one manage-native-encryption-at-rest.md documents, and the two never cross-reference each other despite both being rooted in the identical encryption:master-password. Native encryption at rest's hierarchy (encryption-at-rest key -> DEK -> bucket/audit/config/log data) is about to appear in six of this batch's other records; this page's hierarchy (master password -> master key (PBKDF2) -> data key -> system secrets, defined here as 'system-essential passwords and certificates') is a separate mechanism with its own separate terms (master key, data key) that only coincidentally share the word 'key' with encryption-at-rest's DEK/KEK vocabulary. Whether 'system secrets' (passwords/certificates) and the config/audit/log data manage-native-encryption-at-rest.md's master-password path protects are the SAME underlying protected data, described from two different subsystems, or genuinely disjoint, cannot be determined from either page - no source states the relationship either way. Flagged as a real candidate for SME review rather than silently merged or silently left looking like two unrelated systems; per the standing rule, kept as two concept families (encryption:* vs secrets:*) until a source states otherwise.
